findings.note: front : back reads the same as back : front — an axis has two ends, not a start

I could tell these four garment-fit terms belonged together, but had no firm way to determine whether the intended pairing was collar/waistband vs shoulder/cuff, or some other split (e.g., top-of-garment vs bottom-of-garment), so the exact relationship and order here was a guess.

notes:
set-directional fails both integrity and playtest checks: the axis is symmetric (no inherent order) and the two pairs mix grains (torso-span vs arm-span), making the split unguessable. Needs new pairs with a genuine directional, same-grain axis.
- set-directional: Collar:waistband spans a whole garment top-to-bottom while shoulder:cuff spans only the arm/sleeve, so the pairs aren't the same grain; and the axis itself is symmetric (front:back reads the same reversed), so order can't be inferred.
  Try: Replace with two pairs at the same garment-region grain and give the relationship an inherent direction, e.g. 'neckline : hem' :: 'shoulder seam : sleeve hem' (both full top-to-bottom spans of a garment section), with label specifying direction like 'top edge : bottom edge of the same section'
  Or: Use a non-spatial but ordered pairing instead, e.g. 'raw hem : finished hem' :: 'basted seam : sewn seam' (before-state : after-state), which has a necessary direction unlike a symmetric axis
  Or: Narrow both pairs to sleeve construction only: 'shoulder seam : cuff' :: 'armhole : sleeve hem' so both are strictly arm-region top-to-bottom spans, then relabel to 'the start and end of a sleeve's construction, in sewing order'
Do not change: set-agent-instrument, set-prevention, set-representation — no allowlisted finding touches them.
